subject: Outbound egress fingerprint validation and firewall rule digest for Catalyst Biomed
messages:
From: Ian McAllister <ian.mcallister@catalystbiomed.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: security@catalystbiomed.com
Date: 2027-12-08T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Private endpoint egress — allowlist & validation asks

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our security team has a few specific asks so we can sign off on the private endpoint deployment in our VPC:

- Canonical list of outbound IP addresses (and if they are ephemeral or static) for the control plane + runtime.
- FQDNs / hostnames your services use and whether TLS SNI or DNS TLS are required.
- Firewall rule snippets we can drop into our perimeter appliance (Palo Alto) and a minimal port/protocol matrix.
- Any mTLS or client cert requirements for the control-plane callbacks to our telemetry endpoints.
- Evidence artifacts for attestation (sample flow logs, cert thumbprints, or a small proof bundle).

We need these items for our SOC intake and to provide to procurement before the onboarding window (targeting 2028-01-10). Can you provide an initial manifest and sample rules?

Thank you — want to keep this tight, happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

Ian
Security Engineer, Catalyst Biomed

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ian McAllister <ian.mcallister@catalystbiomed.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-09T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — allowlist & validation asks

Ian —

Appreciate the clear list. I've compiled an initial manifest and a set of firewall snippets for your team to validate. High-level notes:

- Redwood Private uses a split-plane model: a control plane (management/telemetry) and a runtime plane (inference). For VPC private endpoints we offer both static reserved egress IPs (recommended for strict allowlists) and ephemeral NAT pools (recommended for scale).
- Default recommendation: allow the static control-plane egress block for management (sensible for SOC sign-off) and pin runtime calls to the ephemeral pool with a short-lived certificate exchange when possible.
- We support TLS with SNI and optional DNS-over-TLS for name resolution. mTLS is supported for control-plane webhooks when customers configure a TLS client cert.

Attachments included: catalyst-egress-manifest-20271208.csv (CSV with IP blocks, purpose, rotation cadence), egress-firewall-snippets-20271209.txt (Palo Alto and iptables snippets), and a small evidence bundle we will add to a follow-up email.

Next steps: David and I added a couple of suggested firewall rules in the snippets file — Jordan can propose NAT behavior for your gateway if you want to keep runtime IPs ephemeral but still provide an auditable mapping.

If helpful, we can lock in a 30-minute call Thursday to walk through the manifest and capture any missing artifacts for your SOC pack.

Thanks,
Naomi
Security & Partner Ops, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: catalyst-egress-manifest-20271208.csv (attachment stub)
Attachment: egress-firewall-snippets-20271209.txt (attachment stub)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Ian McAllister <ian.mcallister@catalystbiomed.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-10T08:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — allowlist & validation asks

Ian — quick add from infra:

1) NAT & Source Translation:
- If you select reserved egress IPs we will advertise a /29 (or aggregated /24 for larger commitments) that you can pin in your firewall. These are static and have a documented rotation policy (rare — standard SLA-backed rotation events are 90+ days).
- If you prefer ephemeral NAT for runtime, we provide a labeled ephemeral pool; each VPC attaches an ephemeral label and we can emit a per-session mapping via audit logs. This mapping is available via an API endpoint for a 48-hour window (useful for post-incident tracing).

2) Recommended minimal firewall snippets (Palo Alto style):
- Allow TCP 443 to runtime.redwood-inference.net (SNI required): source <your VPC>, dest <egress-ip-blocks>, app ssl, profile none
- Allow TCP 443 to control.redwood-inference.net (mTLS optional): source <your VPC>, dest <control-plane-ip-blocks>, app ssl, profile AV
- For telemetry ingestion use: TCP 6514 (syslog over TLS) if you configure remote syslog; otherwise ensure 443 is open for batched telemetry pushbacks.

3) Evidence exports: we can produce a small sample of flow logs + cert thumbprints in a signed ZIP (egress-qa-evidence.zip). We'll redact customer traffic.

Flagging Jordan to propose how the NAT rewrite would appear on your gateway (X-Forwarded-For vs. source-NAT) so you can reconcile with internal logging.

-David

---
Attachment: egress-qa-evidence.zip (attachment stub)

From: Ian McAllister <ian.mcallister@catalystbiomed.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: security@catalystbiomed.com
Date: 2027-12-10T13:11:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — allowlist & validation asks

Thanks Naomi and David — this is very helpful. Two clarifying questions from our SOC lead: 

1) For the ephemeral pool option, can you confirm the maximum dwell time of an IP on our flows before rotation? Our compliance team needs a number to justify patrol automation.
2) If we choose static reserved IPs, do you support per-tenant tagging so we can correlate billing/traffic to a tenant id exported in your logs?

Also — would it be possible to get a sample Palo Alto XML policy snippet (not just human readable rules) that we can drop into our template? The textual snippet is fine for initial review but our ops team prefers an importable artifact.

If it's easier I'll schedule the call Thursday and we can walk the sample artifacts live.

Ian

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ian McAllister <ian.mcallister@catalystbiomed.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-12T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — allowlist & validation asks

Ian — quick answers and delivery plan: 

- Ephemeral dwell time: typical rotation windows are 24—72 hours depending on pool pressure; SLA customers can request tighter rotation policies (we've delivered 12-hour windows for regulated customers on Dedicated). We will include a clear column in the CSV manifest with "rotation_expected_hours" for each IP block.
- Per-tenant tagging for static IPs: yes — logs include tenant_id and route_tag fields that are exported to our audit API and embedded in flow logs. We'll mark that field in the manifest and include a sample JSON query to the audit API in the Drive link.
- Palo Alto XML: attaching a minimal importable XML policy snippet in the Drive link (file: paloalto-import-sample.xml). It includes rules for runtime.redwood-inference.net and control.redwood-inference.net and placeholder tags for your VPC CIDRs.

What I'm sending next:
1) Updated CSV with rotation_expected_hours and tenant_tagging column.
2) Palo Alto XML sample (paloalto-import-sample.xml) uploaded to the Drive link below.
3) A short checklist for SOC ingestion where to place the sample evidence and the API query to pull runtime-to-ip mappings if you choose ephemeral NAT.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1F7egress-manifest
JIRA (tracking): NETOPS-2287

I'll be available for the Thursday 30-min slot — propose 10:00am PT and I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Best,
Naomi
Security & Partner Ops, Redwood Inference
